verdicts.note: General safety profile across six SSRIs.
Panic-disorder efficacy.
Review of gestational antidepressant exposure and spontaneous abortion. Wall 3, cross-file B.5.
STAR*D level-3 switching for remission.
Male zebrafish GnRH and spermatogenesis. Wall 7 — and note the mechanism is exactly the endocrine pathway v5 asserts for humans, evidenced only in fish.

KEY FOR IDENTIFICATION. Infertility-related stress PREDICTS first antidepressant prescription, 10-year register. The reverse channel measured directly rather than hypothesised, and it is the reason a cross-sectional medication-fertility association is uninterpretable.
Preconception DEPRESSION and time-to-pregnancy, couple-based prospective cohort. D.3.a's estimand and B.7's counterfactual baseline; the quantity that must be netted out.
CNS drugs among prescribed medications contributing to male-factor infertility.
SSRI use among Danish women of childbearing age by lifestyle. Directly the exposure-prevalence parameter, in the right age band.
Title names sexual AND fertility effects, but the record carries no abstract and the venue is a journal of psychology critique rather than an empirical outlet. Retrieve before routing.
Hydroxybupropion on human spermatozoa in vitro.
16-year SSRI dispensing before, during and after pregnancy. Documents the discontinuation-at-intention pattern the scope document flags as an exposure-measurement threat.
Maternal, fetal and neonatal risks. Wall 4.
Depressive symptoms and infertility in US women. Cross-sectional NHANES-style; the confounded association in its rawest form.
Age and infertility. A.15's.
Comparative benefits and harms for depression treatment.
Separates disorder-driven from drug-driven sexual dysfunction, which is Wall 1 applied at link 1.

North American prospective study of depression, psychotropic use and SEMEN QUALITY. Same cohort family as W4211211986 but a mechanism outcome, so it does not double-count in the primary cell. No abstract on the record.
FAERS and EudraVigilance disproportionality for drug-induced male infertility. Spontaneous-report ascertainment, so a signal rather than an effect size.
Rush inventory; the abstract states outright that rates vary with method of ascertainment, which is the MEASUREMENT_ASCERTAINMENT finding stated inside a link-1 study.
Trazodone on the HPT axis; animal model. Wall 7.
Wall 4, nursing-practice framing.
Female rats. Wall 7.
Clinical workup timing for female infertility.
TESD frequencies and functional outcomes, SSRIs vs duloxetine.
Paternal SSRI use and offspring autism. Paternal exposure but an offspring outcome; Wall 4.
Inappropriate prescribing in the elderly.
Standardised expected-pregnancy estimates for fecundity. Outcome-side measurement; needed to make TTP estimates commensurable.
Hypoactive sexual DESIRE specifically, in depressed women on SSRIs. Desire rather than orgasm, so it is the link-1 endpoint closest to link 2.
Qualitative dissertation on persistent post-discontinuation sexual side effects, n=9. PSSD; carried for the persistence question, not for an effect size.
Congenital anomalies. Wall 4.
Attentional performance.
Lipopolysaccharide model. Wall 7.
States and measures the core ascertainment fact: incidence in pre-marketing efficacy trials runs several times below systematically-elicited incidence. Also a link-1 estimate.
Intercourse patterns inside time-to-pregnancy studies. The exact parameter link 3 needs, including the timing-behaviour confound.
Environmental SSRI exposure framing. Wall 8, and non-human besides.
Paternal SSRI and offspring ADHD. Wall 4.
Bone health.

KEY RECORD. PRESTO-style North American preconception cohort: male depression AND psychotropic medication use against FECUNDABILITY. Both exposures in one design, which is what Wall 1 demands, and the outcome is a conception hazard rather than a semen parameter.
How to manage SSRI sexual dysfunction.

Fertility and Sterility commentary explicitly on the depression/antidepressant/fertility tangle. No abstract on the record; likely an editorial accompanying a primary study, and worth retrieving for the framing rather than an estimate.
Spontaneous abortion and malformations together; the malformation half is Wall 4 and the loss half cross-files to B.5.
Indian tertiary-centre prescribing pattern. Non-OECD prevalence, thin but rare.
GAD pharmacotherapy algorithm.
AASD pathophysiology review; the management half is OFF_CLINICAL_MANAGEMENT.
Double-blind randomised fixed-dose paroxetine vs citalopram on ejaculation. Randomised evidence on link 1, which is why link 1 will rate well and the chain will not.
Type 2 diabetes in youths.
Anorectal malformations. Wall 4.

Antidepressant use and ELECTIVE TERMINATION. Routed out: the outcome is induced abortion, which is A.4's estimand. Flagged rather than merely dropped, because a medication-driven termination decision would be a births channel and nobody in this literature has framed it as one. It earns no recall credit here.
Wuhan antidepressant use trend 2006-2012. Chinese prevalence, and the level is the point.
Tricyclic dosing during childbearing.
Male reproductive health and the environment special issue. B.2/B.6 framing.
Nonvertebral fractures.
Kaiser youth trends 1994-2003 across antidepressants, lithium and anticonvulsants. Below reproductive age at the start of the window but documents the cohort now in it.
PREVENT study, acute and continuation phases.
Trial bias in efficacy research. Relevant to how link-1 side-effect rates are under-ascertained in trials, but the estimand is efficacy.
2025 scoping review of antidepressants and the FEMALE reproductive system. The female-side channel-1 record the reconnaissance could not find; LEAKAGE WALL applies.
Birth defects. Wall 4.
Clinician-administered side-effect scale in a naturalistic setting.

Human Reproduction review of SSRI use in INFERTILE women, covering the impact on fertility. Female primary-cell channel-1 seed; LEAKAGE WALL applies. Population is selected on subfecundity, so transport to a general population needs an argument.
